setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.caption: Channel 1 has patterns 1 and 2 merged in All mode (both patterns contribute their notes, with pattern 1 supplying velocity) in D major. Check the four-step result on port 1/channel 1: MIDI 66, 64, 69, 67 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97. Channel 2 has not been set up yet.
steps.title: Checkpoint 1 — hear the existing phrase

steps.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1), open Channel tasks > Device with E1/E2 and K3. Check the screen header reads DEVICE CH02. A channel is the numbered MIDI route on an output.
steps.title: Checkpoint 2 — select channel 2

steps.caption: On Device, choose the same device on port 2 and MIDI channel 2, then press K3 to apply. A port is a MIDI output; the channel number is the route the receiver listens to. Assign pattern 2 at (2,2), set its range to steps 1–4 by holding step 1 and tapping step 4, then check Merge modes shows CH02 and Patterns 02 and slot (2,2) remains lit.
steps.title: Checkpoint 3 — assign a separate output

steps.caption: Open Channel tasks > Masks and press K3. Check the screen reads Note Masks for CH02; this is where the channel's note values and held-step masks are edited.
steps.title: Checkpoint 4 — open channel 2 Masks

steps.caption: On Masks, hold step 3 and play MIDI note 76 at velocity 90; a mask is an override stored on the held step. Release the key and step. Select channel 1 at (1,1), press Play (1,8), then Stop. Check the MIDI strip: port 1/channel 1 keeps MIDI 66, 64, 69, 67 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97; port 2/channel 2 plays MIDI 69 (A) on step 1 and MIDI 76 on step 3. The complete route for this scene is [MIDI Keyboard Input](#midi-keyboard-input/workflow-second-channel).
steps.title: Checkpoint 5 — add one note and verify both routes
